title: Phased decommissioning plan for adapter endpoints with automated client guidance and rollback gating
creator: Leah Chen
description: This ticket defines the PRD and acceptance criteria for a phased sunset of the adapter-style endpoints (adapter/*) used by older SDKs and third-party integrations. The goal is to retire adapter endpoints in a way that minimizes customer disruption by providing automated client guidance (SDK updates, opt-in redirect headers, and a migration CLI), clear telemetry gates for rollout, and explicit rollback criteria. This document covers scope, timeline, stakeholder responsibilities, communication cadence, and measurable success criteria.
background: Adapter endpoints were introduced as a compatibility layer to bridge legacy client integrations while we developed the unified inference surface. Over time this layer has become a maintenance burden (extra routing, duplicate telemetry, and performance regressions). Product decided to consolidate onto the unified API surface to simplify routing, improve observability, and reduce long-tail operational cost.
goals: Shut down adapter/* endpoints without material breakage for 95% of active customers
Provide an automated migration path via SDK updates and an optional CLI that rewrites customer requests to the unified API during a grace period
Ensure rollout is gated by telemetry (error rate, successful migrated requests) and has rapid rollback mechanics
Update public docs, SDKs and generate per-customer migration reports before final cutover
out_of_scope: Full rewrite of third-party integrations; one-off manual migrations for customers with on-prem private deployments (handled via support engagements). Internal runtime kernel changes unrelated to routing are out of scope for this ticket.
success_metrics: <=1% customer-reported functional regressions in 30 days post-final shutdown
>=95% of eligible traffic migrated via automated SDK/CLI within grace period
No increase in platform P99 latency attributable to migration routing during rollout windows
Telemetry gates satisfied (see telemetry_gates) for each phase before promoting rollout
acceptance_criteria: Public docs updated with migration guides and examples for all official SDKs
SDK clients (JS, Python, Go) ship automated version that emits deprecation warnings and optional auto-migration toggle
Migration CLI and server-side redirect mapping service provisioned and documented
Canary region rollout demonstrates stable error rates (<0.5% increase) and successful migrations >=98% over 72h
Support playbook and batch migration runbook published and reviewed by CS and Support
Security review completed and any KMS/HSM implications addressed
migration_timeline: 2026-03-15: Publish PRD and open cross-team RFC (this ticket)
2026-03-22 to 2026-04-05: SDK update development and migration CLI prototype
2026-04-06 to 2026-04-20: Internal canary rollout (10% of internal test tenants) and runbook dry-run
2026-04-21 to 2026-05-05: Customer beta cohort opt-in with targeted email campaigns
2026-05-06 to 2026-05-12: Broad slow roll (region-by-region) if telemetry gates pass
2026-05-15: Final shutdown of adapter/* endpoints for hosted customers (on-prem customers by agreement)
rollout_steps: Create SDK releases that default to warning-only mode and offer an opt-in auto-migrate flag
Deploy redirect mapping service that records original request signature and maps to unified endpoints
Enable CLI tool for customers to validate request/response equivalence locally
Open small beta cohort and run a 2-week migration with daily telemetry review
Stage broad roll by region with 48-hour observation windows between regions
Execute final cutover and monitor support queues for 72 hours with staffed escalation path
telemetry_gates: Pre-rollout baseline: adapter endpoint error rate <0.2% for last 14 days
Canary gate: successful automated migrations >=98% and no P95 latency regression >5%
Beta gate: customer-reported regressions <=1 per 1,000 migrated customers in beta cohort
Pre-cutover gate: system-wide error budget remaining >=70% and SLO health green for 7 consecutive days
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Large customers with custom proxies may fail automated migration. Mitigation: Schedule manual account outreach and offer migration runbooks and support sessions.
Risk: Redirect mapping could introduce latency. Mitigation: Benchmark mapping service, add caching, and ensure canary latency gates are strict.
Risk: Incomplete telemetry coverage for some older SDK versions. Mitigation: Add server-side exploratory logging for unidentified user agent strings and reach out to owners.
Risk: Regulatory or contractual customers (on-prem) require extended timelines. Mitigation: Create exception process and support contracts for negotiated cutover dates.
qa_checks: Automated integration tests verifying request/response parity for 20 canonical prompt shapes
Load test redirect mapping at 2x expected peak traffic with <3% error rate
SDK backwards-compat tests ensuring warning-only mode does not change response bodies
Manual 3rd-party integration smoke tests for top 10 customers by volume
rollback_plan: During rollout windows, if telemetry gate fails, immediately disable auto-migration flag on server side and revert redirect mappings to passive mode
Reissue SDK advisory and re-open adapter/* endpoints for affected regions while support triages
Run targeted rollback for customers showing broken integrations and coordinate mitigation with Support and Account teams
Perform post-mortem and require 72-hour stability before re-attempting promotion
notes: Aim for a low-friction, measurable migration that leverages our SDK footprint. Avoid hard shutdowns without documented customer agreements. Coordinate communication with Marketing for blog/announcements and with Account Management for high-touch customers.
